questions.question_text:
Spinner $A$ has two equal sectors labelled $P$ and $Q$.
Spinner $B$ has three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$.
Both spinners are spun and Spinner $A$'s result is written first.
The empty array below is set up to record the outcomes.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P & & & \\ Q & & & \end{array}$
Which list shows every outcome?

options.why: Wrote each outcome with Spinner $B$ first, although the question records Spinner $A$'s result first.
Stopped after five outcomes by adding $2+3$ instead of pairing every $A$ result with every $B$ result.
Filled only the $P$ row of the array and left out every outcome in which Spinner $A$ shows $Q$.

questions.solution_text:
Every result of Spinner $A$ pairs with every result of Spinner $B$, so each of the $2$ rows holds $3$ cells.
The outcomes are $(P,1)$, $(P,2)$, $(P,3)$, $(Q,1)$, $(Q,2)$ and $(Q,3)$.

questions.question_text:
A coin is tossed and a spinner with three equal sectors labelled $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ is spun.
The array records the outcomes, with the coin down the side.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & X & Y & Z \\ \hline H & (H,X) & (H,Y) & (H,Z) \\ T & (T,X) & & (T,Z) \end{array}$
Which outcome belongs in the empty cell?

options.why: Kept the correct row heading $T$ but took the column heading from the column to the left of the empty cell instead of its own column.
Kept the correct column heading $Y$ but took the row heading from the row above the empty cell instead of its own row.
Copied the entry of the filled cell diagonally above and to the left instead of reading the empty cell's own row and column headings.

questions.solution_text:
The empty cell sits in the $T$ row and the $Y$ column, and each cell pairs its row heading with its column heading.
The missing outcome is $(T,Y)$.

questions.question_text:
Spinner $A$ has four equal sectors labelled $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$.
Spinner $B$ has three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$.
Both spinners are spun and every outcome is recorded in the array below.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline A & & & \\ B & & & \\ C & & & \\ D & & & \end{array}$
How many outcomes does the experiment have?

options.why: Added the results of the two stages, $4+3$, instead of pairing every $A$ result with every $B$ result.
Used four results at both stages, $4 \times 4$, although the second spinner has only three sectors.
Multiplied the number of columns by itself, $3 \times 3$, instead of rows by columns.

questions.solution_text:
Every cell of the array holds one outcome, and the array has $4$ rows and $3$ columns.
Number of outcomes $= 4 \times 3$
$= 12$

questions.question_text:
A spinner has three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$.
It is spun twice and the results are recorded in order.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline 1 & (1,1) & (1,2) & (1,3) \\ 2 & (2,1) & (2,2) & (2,3) \\ 3 & (3,1) & (3,2) & (3,3) \end{array}$
Which list gives all the outcomes in which the second spin shows a larger number than the first?

options.why: Listed the outcomes in which the first spin is larger, reading each pair the wrong way round.
Included the outcomes with two equal numbers, although the second spin must be strictly larger.
Only checked the pairs whose larger number is $3$, so $(1,2)$ was missed.

questions.solution_text:
Read each cell and compare its column heading with its row heading.
The second number is larger in $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$ and $(2,3)$.

options.why: Read the top branch of the spinner stage, labelled $1$, instead of the branch labelled $2$ named in the question.
Wrote the coin result first, although the spinner is the first stage of the tree and is recorded first.
Read the top branch labelled $1$ instead of the branch labelled $2$, and also wrote the second-stage coin result before the spinner result.

questions.solution_text:
The branch labelled $2$ splits into the two coin results, and the spinner result is written first.
The outcomes are $(2,H)$ and $(2,T)$.

options.why: Counted every complete path in the tree instead of only the paths whose second branch is $2$.
Counted the three sectors of Spinner $B$ instead of the paths that end in $2$.
Counted only the first branch labelled $2$ and missed the matching branch lower in the tree.

questions.solution_text:
Read the outcome at the end of each complete path and pick out those containing a $2$.
They are $(R,2)$ and $(B,2)$, so $2$ outcomes contain the number $2$.

options.why: Added the two results of the extra spin to the four two-spin outcomes instead of splitting each path in two.
Multiplied the four two-spin outcomes by the three spins instead of by the two results of the extra spin.
Doubled the number of paths twice more, as if a fourth spin had also been added.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the four complete paths splits into the two results of the third spin.
Number of outcomes $= 2 \times 2 \times 2$
$= 8$

questions.question_text:
Six cards showing the letters $P$, $L$, $A$, $N$, $E$ and $T$ are in a bag.
One card is drawn, then a second card is drawn without replacing the first.
The crosses show the cells that cannot occur.
$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} & P & L & A & N & E & T \\ \hline P & \times & & & & & \\ L & & \times & & & & \\ A & & & \times & & & \\ N & & & & \times & & \\ E & & & & & \times & \\ T & & & & & & \times \end{array}$
How many outcomes does the experiment have?

options.why: Counted every cell of the array, including the six crossed cells that cannot occur.
Counted each pair of letters once, treating $(P,L)$ and $(L,P)$ as the same outcome.
Added the six results of the first draw to the five of the second instead of multiplying them.

questions.solution_text:
The array has $6$ rows and $6$ columns, and the $6$ cells on the diagonal are crossed out.
Number of outcomes $= 36 - 6$
$= 30$

questions.question_text:
A two-stage experiment is recorded in the array below.
The same experiment is now drawn as a tree diagram, with the stage down the side of the array as the first stage.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline P & (P,1) & (P,2) & (P,3) \\ Q & (Q,1) & (Q,2) & (Q,3) \\ R & (R,1) & (R,2) & (R,3) \\ S & (S,1) & (S,2) & (S,3) \end{array}$
How many branches leave the start of the tree, and how many complete paths does the tree have?

options.why: Took the column stage as the first stage, so counted its $3$ results as the branches leaving the start.
Added the sizes of the two stages, $4+3=7$, to count the paths instead of multiplying them.
Took the column stage as the first stage and also added the two stage sizes, $3+4=7$, instead of multiplying them.

questions.solution_text:
The row stage has $4$ results, so $4$ branches leave the start, and each of them splits into the $3$ column results.
Number of paths $= 4 \times 3$
$= 12$

questions.question_text:
A spinner has five equal sectors labelled $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$.
It is spun twice and the results are recorded in order.
How many of the outcomes show two different letters?

options.why: Counted every outcome, including the five in which the same letter is spun twice.
Counted each pair of different letters once, treating $AB$ and $BA$ as the same outcome.
Counted the outcomes in which the same letter appears twice instead of those with two different letters.

questions.solution_text:
The array for two spins has $5$ rows and $5$ columns.
Total outcomes $= 5 \times 5$
$= 25$
The outcomes with the same letter twice are the $5$ cells on the diagonal.
Outcomes with two different letters $= 25 - 5$
$= 20$
